title: Short Stuff: The Javelina
summary: Short Stuff episode on the javelina (collared peccary), prompted by a listener-style pick from Josh after a Royal Tenenbaums scene. The hosts cover how javelinas differ from true pigs: they are only distantly related, are New World animals from North, Central and South America while pigs are Old World, have a scent gland near the base of the tail used for marking territory, have poor eyesight but a good sense of smell, and have a distinctive nose said to be as individual as a fingerprint. They discuss their size (about two feet tall, up to fifty pounds), herd behavior, reputation for ferocity (mostly defensive of territory and young), the viral Tucson video, their even-toed hoof structure, mostly herbivorous diet, and interactions with dogs. Tangents include wild horses on Cumberland Island, Georgia, and a documentary about horses.

segments.title: Introduction and the Royal Tenenbaums pick
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short on the javelina, explaining his interest began with a Royal Tenenbaums scene. He notes javelinas are only distantly related to pigs and are collared peccaries, and Chuck mentions regional sightings in the South.

segments.title: Javelina size, appearance and differences from pigs
segments.summary: The hosts describe javelinas as about two feet tall and up to fifty pounds, with no visible tail, herd behavior unlike pigs, a scent gland near the tail base used for marking, and a nose that is distinctive enough to act like a fingerprint. They note pigs are Old World animals while javelinas are New World, from North, Central and South America. A viral Tucson video is mentioned.

segments.title: Senses, musk and the danger of getting close
segments.summary: The hosts discuss javelinas' strong sense of smell and musky odor, the 'skunk pig' nickname, and the misconception that they are rodents. Javelinas have poor eyesight, seeing about thirty feet, so humans can get close, which is risky.

segments.title: Commercial break
segments.summary: A break in the episode, with the hosts returning after the commercial.

segments.title: Javelina reputation for ferocity and hoof structure
segments.summary: Experts say javelinas are defensive, mostly protecting territory and young, and that the reputation for ferocity may be undeserved. The hosts explain that javelinas are even-toed ungulates, bearing weight on the third and fourth toes, and contrast this with horses and rhinoceroses, mentioning a horse documentary.

segments.title: Wild horses, Cumberland Island and digression
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss Cumberland Island, Georgia and its wild horses, and a horse documentary's section on domestication, followed by a tangent about a repeated topic and the 'Stuff You Should Know Effect' joke.

segments.title: Javelina diet and dog interactions
segments.summary: The javelina is described as mainly herbivorous, eating roots, fruits and plants, though it will eat meat occasionally. Javelinas may chase dogs they see as coyotes, and a video shows a javelina playing with a dog. Josh suggests searching 'javelina dog play'.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up the short and credit the production company.
